findings.reason: pageLabel re-implements the label chain that pages-link-indexer.ts:493 extractTitle already has (frontmatter.title -> first H1 -> fallback). The two now give different fallbacks (full relPath here, basename without .md there), so the same page can carry two different labels depending on whether it comes from GET page-detail or from the link index. The H1 regex also matches a `# comment` line inside a fenced code block that comes before the real H1. That is also true of the existing helper, but sharing one helper would keep the two in step.

The literal frontmatterRaw write-back is fixed only in the two anchor write-back sites. Other server-side rewrites of a page still write { frontmatter: current.frontmatter, body } and so drop a broken header block silently: the edit_section batch (page-write.ts:1815), reference propagation on rename (references.ts:200/212/242) and section ops (sections.ts:222/231). This is outside the editor-save path the goal names, but it is the same data-loss mechanism. A small shared helper (read -> write that keeps frontmatterRaw) would close it everywhere and would replace the duplicated ternary in anchor-injection.ts and section-indexer.ts.
